I'm settling on the answer now, keeping it to short sentences with steps as the only list. I'll cite the runtime view page, and I'm weighing whether to point to the rules page as well, though the tool loop is already in its diagram. I may just answer and offer to walk through the guards or the registration code.

The engine runs a tool call inside a loop. The model asks for a tool, the engine runs it through the guards, and the result goes back to the model. This repeats for up to 10 rounds per message, then the model answers.

Each call goes through `ToolCallGuards.InvokeAsync`, which does three things:

- It logs the call.
- It runs the tool.
- It checks the result.

A result over 50,000 characters is summarised by a separate model call with no tools. A reply cut off by the output limit has incomplete tool arguments, so that call is never run. The model is asked to write large content in chunks instead. If a tool throws, the exception message goes back to the model, so it can correct itself.

On the last round, the engine keeps the tool list on the request but sets tool use to none. The model then answers in text. Every request is priced in the ledger, one record per round.

Tools are registered per session. Each public instance method on a pack's tool class becomes a tool, named after the method.

The page's diagram shows this loop. The guards are on the rules section.
